sections.name: Finance, Accounting & Audit Integration
sections.outcome: Transform economic events and financial records into reliable operational, reporting, compliance, assurance, valuation, and investment decisions while preserving traceability among assumptions, evidence, calculations, and conclusions.
excludes: general legal analysis without a financial reporting or transaction purpose
pure economics problems without an organizational financial decision
clerical document formatting without financial reasoning

sample_tasks.instruction: Given one credit sale followed by customer payment, identify its effects on the invoice, ledger balances, cash records, and one relevant control.

For a company with transaction records, draft statements, tax schedules, control exceptions, financing alternatives, and an investment portfolio, produce an integrated analysis that reconciles the records, corrects reporting issues, assesses controls and filing effects, values the alternatives, and recommends supported actions.

sections.name: Accounting Records & Financial Reporting
sections.outcome: Convert transactions into balanced accounting records, reconcile independent evidence, complete period-end adjustments, and produce internally consistent financial statements.

sample_tasks.instruction: For a cash purchase of supplies, identify the accounts affected, their debit or credit direction, and the resulting accounting-equation change.

Turn a month of transaction evidence into journal entries and ledgers, resolve discrepancies against bank and subsidiary records, post period-end adjustments, and prepare a balanced set of financial statements.

sections.name: Transaction Analysis & Journal Entries
sections.outcome: Identify the economic substance of routine and adjusting events and record balanced entries in the correct accounts and periods.

sample_tasks.instruction: Record a cash purchase of equipment and state how the entry changes assets, liabilities, and equity.
Prepare dated journal entries for a set of sales, purchases, prepayments, accruals, depreciation, returns, and financing transactions, explaining the recognition and period assignment of each.

sections.name: Ledger Posting & Trial-Balance Integrity
sections.outcome: Post journal entries to account ledgers, calculate balances, and diagnose or correct trial-balance errors without changing valid economic events.

sample_tasks.instruction: Post one balanced journal entry to two T-accounts and calculate their updated balances.
Post a batch of journal entries to general and subsidiary ledgers, produce a trial balance, locate the causes of an imbalance and inconsistent control-account totals, and provide correcting entries.

sections.name: Account Reconciliation & Discrepancy Resolution
sections.outcome: Compare ledger balances with independent records, explain timing and error differences, and produce supported corrections or reconciling items.
excludes: portfolio position reconciliation requiring market-risk analysis

sample_tasks.instruction: Classify a deposit in transit as a bank-side or book-side reconciling item and show the resulting adjusted balance.

Reconcile a cash ledger to a bank statement and a receivables control account to customer balances, distinguish timing differences from errors, and prepare supported correcting entries and an outstanding-item schedule.

sections.name: Period-End Close & Financial Statements
sections.outcome: Complete a period-end close by deriving adjustments from reconciled records and producing linked, classified, and internally consistent financial statements.

sample_tasks.instruction: Using a reconciled ledger and one documented unpaid expense, post the closing-date accrual and carry it into an adjusted trial balance.

Complete the close for an entity from its trial balance and reconciliation schedules, post supported accrual, deferral, depreciation, and error adjustments, and prepare linked income, balance-sheet, cash-flow, and equity statements.

sections.name: Billing, Invoicing & Payment Operations
sections.outcome: Translate commercial terms and delivery evidence into accurate invoices, manage receivables, and apply or resolve payments with a complete transaction trail.

sample_tasks.instruction: Calculate the subtotal, discount, tax, and amount due for one fulfilled order using stated commercial terms.

Process an order-to-cash case by validating fulfillment, issuing an accurate invoice, updating the receivable and aging, applying a partial remittance, and resolving a short payment with an auditable record.

sections.name: Invoice & Credit-Document Production
sections.outcome: Create and validate invoices and credit documents whose quantities, prices, taxes, terms, parties, and supporting references agree with authorized transaction evidence.
excludes: revenue-recognition judgments not determined by billing evidence

sample_tasks.instruction: Calculate the amount due on a single delivered line item after a stated percentage discount and tax rate.

Prepare an invoice for a multi-line, partially fulfilled order with tiered discounts, freight, tax, payment terms, and supporting references, then issue the necessary credit document for a documented return.

sections.name: Receivables Aging & Collections
sections.outcome: Maintain accurate receivable status, age open balances, prioritize collection activity, and document resolutions according to payment terms and customer evidence.
includes: allowance inputs from observed collection risk

sample_tasks.instruction: Determine the due date and aging bucket of one unpaid invoice from its date, terms, and reporting date.

Build an aging schedule from invoices, credits, disputes, and receipts; identify overdue and high-risk balances; and propose prioritized, evidence-based collection actions without pursuing amounts that are not yet due.

sections.name: Payment Application & Exception Resolution
sections.outcome: Match receipts and disbursements to obligations, allocate partial or aggregated payments, and resolve discrepancies, refunds, reversals, and unapplied cash without losing traceability.

sample_tasks.instruction: Apply one customer payment that exactly references two open invoices and state the remaining balances.

Apply a batch remittance across invoices, credits, discounts, and a short payment, isolate the unexplained difference, and document the receivable updates, refund or follow-up action, and unresolved amount.

sections.name: Tax & Regulatory Filing Preparation
sections.outcome: Determine a filing's applicable scope, calculate reportable amounts from financial records, and assemble a reconciled, reviewable submission package under supplied rules.
excludes: regulatory compliance unrelated to financial filings

sample_tasks.instruction: Given an entity type, location, activity, and a supplied filing rule, determine whether one return or schedule is required.

Using supplied jurisdictional rules and a closed ledger, determine filing obligations, calculate taxable amounts and liabilities, prepare the required return schedules, reconcile them to the books, and identify review and submission actions.

sections.name: Filing Scope & Tax Classification
sections.outcome: Apply supplied tax or reporting rules to classify an entity, transaction, period, and jurisdiction and determine the required filings and treatments.
excludes: filling forms before scope is established

sample_tasks.instruction: Apply one stated threshold rule to decide whether an entity must file in a jurisdiction.

Classify an entity and a set of cross-jurisdiction transactions under supplied rules, identify applicable returns, periods, rates, exemptions, and information requirements, and explain each classification from the facts.

sections.name: Tax-Base & Liability Computation
sections.outcome: Convert classified book amounts into a tax or regulatory base and calculate the resulting liability, credits, payments, and balance under supplied rules.
includes: interest and penalty calculations when rules are supplied
excludes: deciding filing scope from incomplete facts

sample_tasks.instruction: Starting from one classified book expense, apply a supplied deductibility rule to calculate its adjustment to the tax base.

Starting from book income and classified transactions, calculate the filing-period tax base, apply supplied rates, limitations, credits, and payments, and derive the liability or refund with a transparent adjustment schedule.

sections.name: Return Assembly, Reconciliation & Filing Controls
sections.outcome: Place computed amounts into the correct return structure, reconcile every material total to books and supporting schedules, and prepare a controlled filing package.
excludes: creating tax classifications or liability calculations from scratch

sample_tasks.instruction: Given a finalized liability computation and reconciled ledger total, place one amount on the specified return schedule and record its supporting reference.

Assemble a return package from completed computations, reconcile form lines and supporting schedules to the ledger and payments, investigate inconsistencies, and produce a filing-readiness checklist with unresolved items.

sections.name: Audit & Internal Controls
sections.outcome: Assess financial-process risks, evaluate and test controls and balances, and communicate evidence-based assurance conclusions and remediation priorities.
excludes: operating routine controls as the process owner

sample_tasks.instruction: For one cash-disbursement process, identify a plausible misstatement risk and the financial assertion it threatens.

Plan and execute a focused audit of a revenue-and-cash process by assessing risks and materiality, documenting controls, selecting and evaluating control and substantive tests, and reporting supported conclusions and remediation priorities.

sections.name: Risk, Assertions & Materiality
sections.outcome: Translate process and financial-statement facts into scoped risks, affected assertions, materiality judgments, and prioritized audit attention.

sample_tasks.instruction: Given an unrecorded supplier invoice near period end, identify the threatened financial-statement assertion.

For a company and its draft statements, set and justify materiality, identify and rank account- and process-level misstatement risks, connect each to assertions, and define the areas requiring further work.

sections.name: Control Design & Walkthrough Evaluation
sections.outcome: Design or evaluate controls that address identified financial risks, including their objective, owner, frequency, evidence, precision, and segregation of duties.
excludes: generic policy writing without a stated risk

sample_tasks.instruction: For one identified duplicate-payment risk, specify a control objective and a single control that directly addresses it.

Map a transaction process, evaluate whether its controls cover the assessed risks and assertions, identify design and implementation gaps, and redesign the control set with clear owners, evidence, frequency, and segregation.

sections.name: Control Operating-Effectiveness Testing
sections.outcome: Select and perform evidence-based tests that determine whether designed controls operated consistently and precisely over the period.
excludes: direct testing of account balances as the primary objective

sample_tasks.instruction: Given a monthly review control and its documented design, identify one item of evidence that would show the control operated for a selected month.

Design and document an operating-effectiveness test for a control population, select appropriate items, evaluate the supplied evidence and exceptions, and conclude whether reliance is supported for the period.

sections.name: Substantive Financial Testing
sections.outcome: Design and evaluate analytical and detail procedures that directly test material balances, transaction classes, and disclosures against relevant assertions.
excludes: legal compliance audits without financial assertions

sample_tasks.instruction: For an assessed completeness risk in accounts payable, choose whether tracing or vouching is the appropriate direction and identify the evidence to start from.

Design and evaluate substantive procedures for a material balance using the assessed risks and assertions, analyze supplied confirmations, documents, cutoff items, and exceptions, and quantify detected and projected misstatement.

sections.name: Audit Conclusions, Findings & Remediation
sections.outcome: Integrate control and substantive evidence, assess exceptions against risk and materiality, and communicate proportionate conclusions, findings, and corrective actions.

sample_tasks.instruction: Given completed control and substantive tests with one corroborated exception, draft a finding that states the condition, criterion, cause, consequence, and action.

Integrate completed control and substantive test results, evaluate the aggregate effect of exceptions against the assessed risks and materiality, classify deficiencies, and issue supported conclusions and prioritized remediation with follow-up criteria.

sections.name: Financial Modeling & Valuation
sections.outcome: Build transparent cash-flow and financial-statement models, test their behavior under uncertainty, and use them to value projects and businesses or securities.
excludes: historical bookkeeping as the main objective
pure economic optimization without financial cash flows

sample_tasks.instruction: Discount one known future cash receipt to present value using a stated rate and timing convention.

Build an integrated forecast from operating assumptions, test scenarios and sensitivities, value a proposed project and the associated business using appropriate cash flows and discount rates, and explain the main value drivers and limitations.

sections.name: Cash Flows & Time Value of Money
sections.outcome: Place financial cash flows on a timeline and consistently compute present values, future values, yields, annuities, and equivalent rates.
excludes: choosing a project from strategic considerations

sample_tasks.instruction: Compute the present value of a single payment due in one year at a stated annual discount rate.
Value an irregular stream containing upfront, periodic, and terminal cash flows under stated compounding conventions, solve for its yield, and reconcile the result using an equivalent effective rate.

sections.name: Forecasting, Scenarios & Sensitivities
sections.outcome: Translate explicit operating and financing assumptions into linked financial forecasts and quantify how uncertainty changes cash, profit, funding needs, and model outputs.
excludes: statistical forecasting detached from financial decisions

sample_tasks.instruction: Forecast next month's revenue and cash receipts from a stated unit-volume assumption, price, and collection lag.

Build a linked operating, profit, working-capital, and cash forecast with threshold-dependent costs and uncertain outcomes, then compare base, downside, and upside scenarios and identify the assumptions driving funding needs.

sections.name: Capital Budgeting & Financing Decisions
sections.outcome: Evaluate projects and financing alternatives using incremental cash flows, discount-rate assumptions, decision metrics, constraints, and scenario evidence.
excludes: strategic claims unsupported by financial analysis

sample_tasks.instruction: Using a completed project cash-flow forecast and stated discount rate, calculate NPV and apply the accept-or-reject rule.

Compare mutually exclusive investment and financing alternatives using incremental forecast cash flows, NPV, IRR, funding constraints, and downside scenarios, reconcile conflicting metrics, and recommend an alternative.

sections.name: Enterprise & Equity Valuation
sections.outcome: Estimate enterprise and equity value from forecast operating performance using defensible cash flows, discount rates, terminal assumptions, and market cross-checks.

sample_tasks.instruction: Using a completed perpetual cash-flow forecast and discount rate, calculate a terminal value and state the condition required for the formula.

Value a business using forecast free cash flow, a justified discount rate and terminal case, bridge enterprise value to equity value, cross-check against supplied market multiples, and present a sensitivity-based valuation range.

sections.name: Trading & Portfolio Analytics
sections.outcome: Measure instrument and portfolio returns, value and assess fixed-income exposures, analyze diversification and performance, and form traceable trade or rebalancing decisions under constraints.
excludes: enterprise operating forecasts as the primary task
predictions unsupported by prices, cash flows, or risk assumptions

sample_tasks.instruction: Calculate the holding-period return on one position from its beginning value, ending value, and cash distribution.

Analyze a multi-asset portfolio by validating positions and returns, valuing its fixed-income exposure, measuring risk and diversification, attributing performance, and recommending trades that meet stated return, risk, liquidity, and cost constraints.

sections.name: Position & Return Measurement
sections.outcome: Convert holdings, prices, cash flows, and corporate actions into consistent position values, gains and losses, and return measures.
excludes: performance attribution to factors or decisions

sample_tasks.instruction: Calculate one security's ending market value and holding-period return including a cash dividend.

Reconstruct positions across purchases, sales, fees, distributions, and a corporate action, then calculate beginning and ending exposure, realized and unrealized gain, and consistent security and portfolio returns.

sections.name: Fixed-Income Valuation & Interest-Rate Exposure
sections.outcome: Value fixed-income cash flows from market yields and measure how timing, yield changes, and instrument features affect price and interest-rate sensitivity.
excludes: general time-value exercises without fixed-income features

sample_tasks.instruction: Price a zero-coupon bond from its maturity value, time to maturity, and quoted yield convention.
For a coupon bond, construct and discount the cash flows, calculate price, yield, Macaulay and modified duration, estimate the effect of a yield change, and explain the approximation's limitations.

sections.name: Portfolio Risk & Diversification
sections.outcome: Aggregate position exposures and return relationships into portfolio risk measures and explain how weights, covariance, concentration, and constraints shape diversification.

sample_tasks.instruction: Using two asset weights, volatilities, expected returns, and their correlation, calculate the portfolio's expected return and volatility.

Calculate and interpret the risk of a multi-asset portfolio from positions and return relationships, identify concentration and factor exposures, quantify marginal risk contributions, and compare feasible diversification changes under stated constraints.

sections.name: Portfolio Performance & Attribution
sections.outcome: Calculate comparable portfolio performance and decompose differences from a benchmark into supported allocation, selection, income, fee, currency, or timing effects.
excludes: instrument valuation as the main objective
narrative performance claims that do not reconcile to total return

sample_tasks.instruction: Chain-link two subperiod returns separated by an external cash flow to obtain a time-weighted return.

Calculate portfolio and benchmark returns across periods, attribute their difference to allocation, selection, currency, income, and fees as applicable, reconcile contributions to active return, and explain the material drivers.

sections.name: Trade & Rebalancing Decisions
sections.outcome: Turn portfolio risk and performance evidence into implementable trades that respect target exposures, liquidity, transaction costs, taxes supplied as constraints, and mandate limits.
excludes: performance measurement or risk estimation performed from scratch

sample_tasks.instruction: Given completed risk and attribution results, adjust one position weight to remove a stated limit breach while preserving the portfolio total.

Using completed risk, exposure, liquidity, and attribution analyses, construct and justify a rebalance trade list that restores mandate limits and target risk, addresses material performance drivers, funds cash needs, and accounts for transaction costs and supplied tax constraints.
